fields.label: Name
fields.help: Unique link identifier. Time-series profiles are matched to this exact name.

fields.label: Carrier
fields.help: Technology carrier (electrolysis, fuel cell, DC, heat pump, …). Drives grouping and canvas colours.

fields.label: From bus
fields.help: Input side: the bus the link draws from. Its capacity and cost are per MW of this input.

fields.label: To bus
fields.help: Output side: the bus that receives the input × efficiency.

fields.label: Port 2 bus
fields.help: Optional extra port 2: with a positive efficiency2 the bus receives energy (CHP heat); with a negative one the link draws from it (a process feed). Leave empty for no port 2.

fields.label: Port 3 bus
fields.help: Optional extra port 3: with a positive efficiency3 the bus receives energy (CHP heat); with a negative one the link draws from it (a process feed). Leave empty for no port 3.

fields.label: Port 4 bus
fields.help: Optional extra port 4: with a positive efficiency4 the bus receives energy (CHP heat); with a negative one the link draws from it (a process feed). Leave empty for no port 4.

fields.label: Process unit
fields.help: Tick when this link is a production step: bus0 is the main input, bus1 the product, the other ports further inputs. A process unit is a fixed client input, not a decision of the plan.

fields.label: Criticality tier
fields.help: How this unit's electrical supply is ranked when it must be cut: safety (priced at VoLL), process_critical (a stop costs a restart), process_flexible (it can stop and catch up from inventory) or deferrable (it shifts within the day).

fields.label: Capacity
fields.help: Rating on the input side (bus0). With extendable ticked, the existing capacity the optimiser starts from.

fields.label: Extendable
fields.help: When ticked, the optimiser chooses the capacity between the minimum and maximum and pays the annualised cost for every MW it adds.

fields.label: Minimum capacity
fields.help: Lower bound on the optimised capacity. Set it to the existing capacity to forbid retirement.

fields.label: Maximum capacity
fields.help: Upper bound on the optimised capacity. Leave empty for no limit.

fields.label: Overnight cost
fields.help: Upfront cost per kW of input capacity, as if built at once without financing. Annualised over the lifetime at the discount rate.

fields.label: Lifetime
fields.help: Technical and economic lifetime. The link retires after its build year plus lifetime.

fields.label: Build year
fields.help: First year the asset operates. With its lifetime, it decides in which investment periods the asset exists.

fields.label: Discount rate
fields.help: The rate this asset's overnight cost is annualised at. Leave empty to use the project's rate from Solver Settings.

fields.label: Capital cost (annualised)
fields.help: Derived: overnight cost × annuity(discount rate, lifetime); fixed O&M is charged on top. Per kW of input.

fields.label: Fixed O&M
fields.help: Fixed operation and maintenance per kW of input per year.

fields.label: Marginal cost
fields.help: Cost per MWh drawn from the input bus.

fields.label: Start-up cost
fields.help: Read-only. PyPSA does not weight a start-up cost by the snapshot or period weighting, so a process unit prices a restart as lost production instead (see grid-to-process ticket 03).

fields.label: Stand-by cost
fields.help: Cost per hour while the unit is on, at any output, including zero.

fields.label: Efficiency
fields.help: Output per unit of input: MWh delivered to bus1 per MWh drawn from bus0 (the COP for a heat pump, above 100 %).

fields.label: Port 2 efficiency
fields.help: Flow on port 2 per unit drawn from bus0. Positive: the port bus receives it (CHP heat, 0.4 = 0.4 MWh per MWh of fuel). Negative: the link draws it from the port bus (a feed, −4.6 = 4.6 per unit of bus0). Read only when bus2 is set.

fields.label: Port 3 efficiency
fields.help: Flow on port 3 per unit drawn from bus0. Positive: the port bus receives it (CHP heat, 0.4 = 0.4 MWh per MWh of fuel). Negative: the link draws it from the port bus (a feed, −4.6 = 4.6 per unit of bus0). Read only when bus3 is set.

fields.label: Port 4 efficiency
fields.help: Flow on port 4 per unit drawn from bus0. Positive: the port bus receives it (CHP heat, 0.4 = 0.4 MWh per MWh of fuel). Negative: the link draws it from the port bus (a feed, −4.6 = 4.6 per unit of bus0). Read only when bus4 is set.

fields.label: Minimum flow
fields.help: Lowest flow as a share of capacity. Negative lets the link run backwards (−100 % for a bidirectional DC line).

fields.label: Maximum flow
fields.help: Highest flow as a share of capacity. A profile uploaded on the Time Series page replaces this value hour by hour.

fields.label: Unit commitment
fields.help: Model on/off decisions with start-ups and minimum up and down times. Adds integer variables: slower, more realistic for thermal plants.

fields.label: Ramp-up limit
fields.help: Largest hour-on-hour increase, as a share of capacity per hour.

fields.label: Ramp-down limit
fields.help: Largest hour-on-hour decrease, as a share of capacity per hour.

fields.label: Minimum up time
fields.help: Hours the unit stays on after a start-up.

fields.label: Minimum down time
fields.help: Hours the unit stays off after a shut-down.

fields.label: Throughput unit
fields.help: Display only: the unit of the product the unit makes per hour, for example t/h. The solve reads the efficiency, not this.

fields.label: Specific energy
fields.help: Display only, derived: electricity per tonne of product, from the efficiency. The solve reads the efficiency, not this.

fields.label: Rated apparent power
fields.help: Rated apparent power of the drive or heater, for the harmonic screen. Leave empty when unknown: the check then reads unknown. It is never taken from the capacity.

fields.label: Harmonic source
fields.help: The drive topology or heater control that sets the unit's harmonic currents. linear declares no harmonic emission. Leave empty when unknown: the check then reads unknown.

fields.label: Harmonic spectrum
fields.help: Harmonic current per order, as order:% of rated current, e.g. 5:20, 7:14. Leave empty to use the demo default for the harmonic source.

fields.label: Spectrum includes the unit's filter
fields.help: Tick when the harmonic spectrum is measured or quoted after the unit's own harmonic filter.

fields.label: Largest power step
fields.help: The largest single change in the unit's apparent power, for the flicker screen. 0 declares a steady load. Leave empty when unknown: the check then reads unknown.

fields.label: Changes per minute
fields.help: How often the power step happens, for the flicker screen: switching on and switching off each count, so one on/off cycle a minute is 2. 0 declares a steady load. Leave empty when unknown: the check then reads unknown.

fields.label: Forced-outage rate
fields.help: Share of time the asset is out on a forced outage, e.g. 5 %. Empty uses the carrier's library default. Read by the adequacy and FMEA analysis only; the dispatch is unaffected.

fields.label: Outage-rate basis
fields.help: What the rate is: FOR (service-hours based, what NERC GADS class averages publish) or EFORd (demand based). They differ materially for peakers with reserve-shutdown hours; the tool stores which one you entered and never converts between them.

fields.label: Mean time to repair
fields.help: How long one forced outage lasts on average. With the rate it implies an event frequency (8760 × rate / MTTR per year).

profile.title: EU RfG (2016/631) and DCC (2016/1388), Continental Europe

rows.requirement: Short-circuit ratio at the PoC
rows.source: Screening rule: an SCR of 3.0, the edge between moderate and strong grids; assumed, not a grid-code value
rows.note: No short-circuit level and inverter capacity at every point of connection, so the SCR is not known

rows.requirement: Load within the energized import (after its efficiency) plus firm gensets and batteries, hour by hour (2030)
rows.source: The connection's capacity and the island requirements' genset N+k and ride-through
rows.note: 2030: binding hour 2030-07-01 00:00:00, hourly-mean load 0 MW against the 60 MW energized import (× 0.99 efficiency) plus 0 MW of firm gensets (no island sidecar: no genset is counted as firm) = 59.4 MW (checked hour by hour; the period's peak is 0 MW); no energization schedule: the connection's capacity; import efficiency from the import Link's efficiency, as entered; fixed loads only (a flexible conversion unit is a decision, not counted); not electric load: nh3_offtake on nh3 (NH3)

rows.requirement: Load ramp rate at the PoC within the connection ramp limit
rows.source: assumed (generic placeholder): 10% of the connection capacity per minute
rows.note: No AI-training load profile on this project, so its ramp, swing and oscillation are not known (a data-centre project created with the AI-training profile has one)

rows.requirement: Power oscillation at the PoC (0.1-2 Hz band) within the limit
rows.source: assumed (generic placeholder): 1 % of the connection
rows.note: No AI-training load profile on this project, so its ramp, swing and oscillation are not known (a data-centre project created with the AI-training profile has one)

rows.requirement: Rapid voltage change at the PoC on the AI-training load step
rows.source: EU RfG (2016/631) and DCC (2016/1388), Continental Europe: not set by RfG/DCC; IEC TR 61000-3-7 indicative planning levels for infrequent rapid voltage changes at HV/EHV are about 3-5 % (not verified against the text here); 3 % used
rows.note: No AI-training load profile on this project, so its ramp, swing and oscillation are not known (a data-centre project created with the AI-training profile has one)

rows.requirement: Rapid voltage change at the PoC on an infrequent event (the whole connection switched)
rows.source: no limit set
rows.note: No limit set: the grid code sets no infrequent rapid-voltage-change tier

rows.requirement: Harmonic voltage distortion at the PoC from the site's drives and heaters
rows.source: EU RfG (2016/631) and DCC (2016/1388), Continental Europe: THD: not set by RfG/DCC; IEC TR 61000-3-6 Table 2 indicative planning level for total harmonic distortion at HV-EHV (not verified against the text here); 3 % used; Individual orders: not set by RfG/DCC; IEC TR 61000-3-6 Table 2 indicative planning levels for individual harmonic voltages at HV-EHV, % of the fundamental (not verified against the text here)
rows.note: THD 0 % (limit 3 %); demo default spectrum for compressor (no vendor spectrum entered); S_k 1000 MVA; a screening estimate (IEC 61000-3-6 summation, U_h = I_h · h / S_k) that ignores network resonance, background distortion and the operator's allocation of the planning level; above the limit a harmonic study is needed

rows.requirement: Flicker severity at the PoC from the site's stepping loads
rows.source: EU RfG (2016/631) and DCC (2016/1388), Continental Europe: Pst: not set by RfG/DCC; IEC TR 61000-3-7 indicative planning level for short-term flicker severity Pst at HV-EHV; a planning level, not an emission limit allocated to this installation (margin overstated); not verified against the text here; Plt: not set by RfG/DCC; IEC TR 61000-3-7 indicative planning level for long-term flicker severity Plt at HV-EHV; a planning level, not an emission limit allocated to this installation (margin overstated); not verified against the text here
rows.note: Pst 0.4482, Plt 0.4482 (limit 0.6); Plt binds: Plt equals Pst for a steady pattern; S_k 1000 MVA; a screening estimate (IEC 61000-3-7 analytic method, d = step / S_k, rectangular steps, Plt = Pst for a steady pattern) that ignores the grid X/R and the operator's allocation of the planning level; units summed with alpha 3 (assumed; units stepping together are not covered); S_k is the entered S_k'' with the IEC 60909 c factor, so d may be understated by up to 1.1; above the limit a flicker-meter study is needed

rows.requirement: Reactive power range at the PoC
rows.source: EU RfG (2016/631) and DCC (2016/1388), Continental Europe: DCC Art. 15(1)(a): not wider than 48 percent of the larger of the maximum import or export capacity (0,9 power factor); the relevant TSO specifies the actual range
rows.note: The project has no island requirements yet

rows.requirement: Frequency support offered by the site's converters
rows.limit: at least one of grid forming, synthetic inertia, frequency containment, fast frequency response
rows.source: Assumed: the scorecard's own expectation for a large connection; the grid code sets no limit
rows.note: The project has no island requirements yet

rows.requirement: Stay connected over the frequency ranges and times
rows.limit: 49.0-51.0 Hz unlimited; 47.5-48.5 Hz and 48.5-49.0 Hz for TSO-specified times (at least 30 min at 47.5-48.5 Hz); 51.0-51.5 Hz 30 min (Continental Europe)
rows.source: EU RfG (2016/631) and DCC (2016/1388), Continental Europe: DCC Art. 12(1) and Annex I, Table 1 (demand facilities); RfG Art. 13(1)(a) Table 2 (generating modules)
rows.note: Needs an RMS study (dynamic; EMT where the code asks for it); it applies to the site; a steady-state screening never passes it

rows.requirement: Withstand a rate of change of frequency
rows.limit: TSO-specified
rows.source: EU RfG (2016/631) and DCC (2016/1388), Continental Europe: RfG Art. 13(1)(b): the rate of change of frequency withstand capability is specified by the TSO
rows.note: Needs an RMS study (dynamic; EMT where the code asks for it); it applies to the site's inverter-based units; a steady-state screening never passes it

rows.requirement: Fault ride-through of the on-site power park modules (BESS, PV)
rows.limit: the TSO's voltage-against-time profile, within the RfG's ranges by module type
rows.source: EU RfG (2016/631) and DCC (2016/1388), Continental Europe: RfG Art. 14(3)(a) (type B) and Art. 16(3)(a) (type D): the TSO specifies the voltage-against-time profile within the RfG's bounds
rows.note: Needs an RMS study (dynamic; EMT where the code asks for it); it applies to the site's inverter-based units; a steady-state screening never passes it

rows.requirement: Limited frequency sensitive mode, over-frequency
rows.limit: droop 2-12 %, threshold 50.2-50.5 Hz (TSO-specified within these)
rows.source: EU RfG (2016/631) and DCC (2016/1388), Continental Europe: RfG Art. 13(2)
rows.note: Needs an RMS study (dynamic; EMT where the code asks for it); it applies to the site's inverter-based units; a steady-state screening never passes it

rows.requirement: A unit that forms the island's voltage
rows.limit: a grid-forming battery or a genset
rows.source: The island study's rule: a grid-forming battery or a genset forms the voltage
rows.note: Not assessed: The project has no island requirements yet

rows.requirement: Loss of load expectation within the reliability goal
rows.source: No LOLE goal in the template's assumptions
rows.note: The project sets no LOLE goal (an ENS cap only, or none)

gr_pass.basis: advisory screening of the saved network and its sidecars; never blocks Run. A fail is a red flag to take to the network operator; unknown means an input is missing, never a pass
